claims.text: Hanja is considered an extinct language because it was the main writing system in Korea until the 20th century, and it is no longer in active use.
Hanja has evolved to have characteristics distinct from modern Korean and modern Chinese, indicating its unique historical development as a language.
Hanja is referred to as a dead language in Korea, highlighting its status as no longer spoken or actively used in contemporary contexts.
